item: Caller identity comes only from a signed session token; the model never supplies it (D39).
A payment is proposed, read back, and confirmed only in a later caller turn; confirm takes no arguments (D23, D24).
A proposal expires after 2 further caller turns or 5 minutes (D73).
A payment whose read-back was interrupted can't be confirmed until it is read back again (D82).
Someone else's account looks exactly like a missing one (D21).
Misheard or unclear speech never reaches the model; it never counts as a caller turn (D60, D69).
Every route is either back-office (admin key), caller (session token) or health, enforced by a test that lists them all (D70, D83).
Per-customer rate limits, conversation caps, a 30-turn handoff and a 15-minute call limit bound cost (D72, D82).
Confirmation only in a later caller turn, counted by code
why: The model could call propose and confirm back to back; code counts turns, the model can't.

item: Hide internal IDs from the model instead of telling it not to say them
why: Prompt rules leak under pressure; data the model never sees can't be read aloud (10/50 to 0/50).

item: Kept a slightly strict judge rather than tuning it to pass
why: A grader tuned until the agent passes stops measuring anything.

item: Speech confidence threshold 0.6, set from measurements
why: No correctly heard clip scored below 0.75; two mishearings scored 0.52 and 0.59.

item: Locked the original REST API behind an admin key after a self-review
why: An anonymous client could read balances and record payments; demonstrated, then closed.

item: Own streaming pipeline (Flux + streaming voice + our agent loop) instead of a managed voice agent
why: Keeps the turn-counting safety rules and the eval on the production path; cheaper per minute.

item: No early 'probably finished' replies
why: A discarded draft could already have run a tool, such as proposing a payment.

item: Track what the caller actually heard, sentence by sentence
why: After an interruption the model is told what got through, and an unheard read-back blocks confirmation.

item: All data is synthetic; no real customers or money.
Eval: 25 scripted conversations x 2 runs, also used to tune v1 and v2; fresh held-out cases are needed before more tuning.
The judge (Claude Haiku) is slightly strict on two phrasings; one remaining failure is that.
Voice checks: 15 phrases, three synthetic voices and one real voice; real phone audio is still to be measured.
Live speed: a handful of calls from one laptop; timings start when the speech service detects the end of the caller's turn, so its own 0.5-1.2 s comes on top.
Mutation testing shows the tests catch the bugs tried, not that no bugs remain.
